pull.title: KAFKA-16304: Report file read errors from SslTransportLayer.transferFrom as such
pull.body:
Follow-up to #23445, under the same ticket (resolved, fix version
4.5.0).

Since #23445, a failed send of fetched records is passed to a handler
that re-reads the region on the scheduler, and the log directory is
offlined only if the re-read fails too. The re-read is needed because
over PLAINTEXT `sendfile` reads the file and writes the socket in one
call, so a disk error and a socket error are the same bare
`IOException`. `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` does not have that
problem: it reads the file with `FileChannel.read`, then encrypts and
writes, so it knows which of the two failed. As discussed on #23445,
this passes that on instead of finding it out again:

* `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` throws a new `FileReadException`, an
  `IOException` with the position of the read, when `FileChannel.read`
  or `FileChannel.size` fails. A `ClosedChannelException`, from a
  deletion or a shutdown, is rethrown as is
  (`FileReadException.ofReadFailure`).
* `TransferableChannel.distinguishesFileReadFailures()` says whether a
  transport does that: true for TLS, false, the default, for
  PLAINTEXT.
* `FileRecords.writeTo` passes to the handler a `FileReadException`
  always, a `ClosedChannelException` never, and any other
  `IOException` only if the transport cannot tell a failed read of the
  file from a failed write to the network channel. A failure of its own
  `channel.size()` call before the transfer becomes a
  `FileReadException` as well, unless it is a `ClosedChannelException`.
* `LocalLog` reports a `FileReadException` as a failure of the log
  directory right away, without re-reading the region. Other failures
  are re-read on the scheduler as before.
* `LogDirFailureChannel.maybeAddOfflineLogDir` logs the error only when
  it takes the log directory offline, so that the failures that follow
  in a failing directory do not flood the log.

Consequences worth stating:

* On TLS listeners a disconnect no longer re-reads the region that was
  being sent. In the test notes, consumers killed mid-fetch over TLS
  for 5 minutes made the scheduler re-read 151 MB without this change
  and nothing with it.
* On TLS listeners a read error now offlines the log directory even if
  the region could be read again by the time of a re-read, e.g. after a
  transient media error. Before, such an error was attributed to the
  socket. This is the criterion `LocalLog` applies to any other
  `IOException`.
* A failed `FileChannel.size()` call on the segment, over either
  transport, is now reported as a read failure without a re-read.
* For every caller of `maybeAddOfflineLogDir`, an error in a log
  directory that is already offline is no longer logged there.
* PLAINTEXT listeners still re-read: `sendfile` cannot tell the two
  apart.
* KRaft snapshots, sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, are still not
  covered.

issue_comments.body:
Test notes for 73fc46a880, on trunk d18f93f985.

Unit tests:

* `SslTransportLayerTest`, `FileRecordsTest` and `LocalLogTest` pass,
  as do `:clients:test` (13757 tests), `:storage:test` (1355 tests),
  checkstyle and spotless. 2 of 5 runs of `:storage:test` failed in
  `TransactionsWithTieredStoreTest` (a timeout, and the test JVM
  exiting), which passes alone 3 times out of 3 here and on trunk. On
  trunk 2 of 3 runs failed in tiered storage integration tests too
  (`TransactionsTest`, `RemoteTopicCrudTest`); see KAFKA-15772.
* Each new or changed test fails when the part of the change it covers
  is undone. 15 such mutations, e.g. `transferFrom` wrapping a closed
  file or a failed socket write, `reportsFileReadFailures()` returning
  false for TLS, a report sharing the re-read's per-directory slot, or
  a failed task not releasing it: each makes the test named for it
  fail.

Cluster: 3 brokers and a controller (KRaft) in Docker on a Linux 6.8
VM. Broker 1 has two log directories, one of them on a `dm-dust`
device. Partition t1-0 has replicas 1, 2 and 3, broker 1 leads it, and
its replica on broker 1 is in the `dm-dust` directory. 20000 records of
512 bytes are produced, then a console consumer reads the partition
from the beginning with an 8 MiB fetch size, over PLAINTEXT or TLS.
`strace -yy` on broker 1 shows which thread reads which file at which
position.

1. Persistent media error: `dm-dust` makes reads of the tail of the
   segment fail on the device. In every run the first read to fail is
   at position 2867200.
   * TLS, trunk: the network thread fails to read position 2867200.
     The scheduler re-reads the region from position 0, 2867200 bytes,
     and fails at 2867200. The directory goes offline.
   * TLS, this change: the same failed read on the network thread, and
     no read of the segment on the scheduler. The directory goes
     offline, with "Failed to read .../00000000000000000000.log at
     position 2867200 while writing 8388608 bytes from position 0 to a
     network channel".
   * PLAINTEXT, both: `sendfile` fails, the re-read on the scheduler
     fails at the same position, and the directory goes offline.
   * In all of them the leader moves to broker 2 and the consumer reads
     all 20000 records.
2. Error gone on the next read: `strace` makes the first read of the
   segment on each network thread of the listener fail with `EIO`, and
   the following reads succeed.
   * TLS, trunk: 3 failed reads, one on each network thread as the
     consumer retried, each followed by a successful re-read of 8 MiB
     on the scheduler. The directory stays online.
   * TLS, this change: the first failed read offlines the directory,
     without a re-read. The consumer reads all 20000 records from
     broker 2.
   * PLAINTEXT, both: as TLS on trunk, the directory stays online.
3. Disconnects, with a healthy disk: 3 TLS consumers read 4 partitions
   led by broker 1, about 200 MB, and are killed after 2 to 8 seconds
   and restarted, for 5 minutes, about 180 times in all.
   * trunk: 4629 reads of segment files on the scheduler, 151 MB.
   * this change: none.
   * No directory went offline in either.

With this change the failed send is still logged as a disconnect, at
DEBUG, now with the `FileReadException`, and the ERROR comes from
`LogDirFailureChannel`. The timings depend on the host, a VM under
load, so I have left them out.

Test notes, continued: the same on macOS 26.7 (Apple Silicon, JDK 17),
with the brokers as local processes, on 73fc46a880 and on trunk
d18f93f985.

* Persistent media error: broker 1's log directory is on a disk image,
  and a 1 MiB band of the image in the middle of the segment is made
  unreadable, so the kernel fails reads of it with EIO. macOS ejects
  the image right after, so every later read fails too. Over TLS,
  trunk re-reads the region on the scheduler, which fails; this change
  offlines the directory without a re-read. Over PLAINTEXT both
  re-read, and the re-read fails. The directory goes offline in all
  four runs, and the consumer reads all 20000 records from broker 2.
* Error gone on the next read, injected by an interposer on `pread`
  and `sendfile` (`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, the macOS stand-in for
  `strace -e inject`): as on Linux, trunk re-reads 8 MiB after each
  failure and keeps the directory online; over TLS this change
  offlines it; over PLAINTEXT both keep it online.
* Disconnects, 3 TLS consumers killed mid-fetch for 5 minutes, about
  180 times: trunk 19497 reads of segment files on the scheduler,
  636 MB; this change none.

On macOS a read fails before the unreadable bytes: with the band at
positions 3129344 to 4177919, `pread` failed at 2129920, and
`sendfile` at 2736128 after reporting progress up to that page. So
`FileReadException.position()` is where the failed read started,
which is not necessarily where the medium failed.

Test notes, continued: OpenBSD 8.0 (arm64, QEMU on macOS) and Windows
10 LTSC (x86-64, QEMU/KVM), both with JDK 17, on 73fc46a880 and on
trunk d18f93f985. Each VM runs one broker and controller, with t1-0 on
a data disk behind QEMU's blkdebug, which fails reads of the disk
sector holding position 4 MiB of the segment with EIO: every read, or
only the first one. A consumer reads the partition from the beginning.

* TLS, every read fails: on both, the network thread's read fails at
  position 4194304. Trunk re-reads the region on the scheduler (3.0 MB
  on OpenBSD, 3.6 MB on Windows), the re-read fails too, and the
  directory goes offline; this change offlines it without a re-read.
* TLS, only the first read fails: on OpenBSD trunk re-reads the region
  successfully and keeps the directory online, while this change
  offlines it. On Windows the disk driver retries the failed read
  (System event 153) and the retry succeeds, so the JVM never sees an
  error, and both keep the directory online.
* PLAINTEXT, every read fails: the JDK writes the file to the socket
  from a memory mapping on both, and the write fails with EFAULT ("Bad
  address") on OpenBSD and WSAEINVAL ("An invalid argument was
  supplied") on Windows rather than with an I/O error. Trunk and this
  change both re-read the region, the re-read fails, and the directory
  goes offline.

No InternalError was thrown in any run.

Windows is on a best-effort basis today. Too different memory management/disk read error handling by the NT kernel and surrounding libraries. 

I will probably take a deeper look after this PR. Maybe, we can bring some better support for Windows.

Test notes for b7708148e2 (the four commits for the review), on trunk
d18f93f985.

Unit tests:

* Checkstyle, spotless and spotbugs for `clients` and `storage` pass.
* A full run of `:clients:test` (13757 tests), `:storage:test` (1355)

* Three other full runs of `:storage:test` (two on be606d42c7, one on
  b7708148e2) each had one test time out after 60 s, every time a
  different one, in tiered storage integration tests:
  `TopicBasedRemoteLogMetadataManagerTest.testTopicDoesNotExist`,
  `TransactionsWithTieredStoreTest.testRecoveryFromEpochOverflow` and
  `.testClassicFencingOnSendOffsets`. Both classes pass alone 3 times
  out of 3 on b7708148e2 and on trunk, and a full run on trunk timed
  out in `TransactionsWithTieredStoreTest.testClassicFencingOnCommit`
  (see KAFKA-15772).
* The new `LogDirFailureChannelTest` fails if the error is logged on
  every call again, and `testFailedReadCheckDoesNotBlockTheNextOne`
  fails if the read check is not finished in a `finally`.

End to end, the scenarios of the earlier notes were rerun on
b7708148e2 on the same four systems, with the jars checked against the
build on each: Linux 6.8 (3 brokers in Docker, `dm-dust` and `strace`),
macOS 26 (3 brokers, an unreadable band of a disk image and an
interposer), OpenBSD 8.0 and Windows 10 (one node in QEMU, `blkdebug`).

| | TLS | PLAINTEXT |
|---|---|---|
| persistent media error, Linux and macOS | read fails on the network thread, no re-read, dir offline | `sendfile` fails, the re-read fails, dir offline |
| persistent media error, OpenBSD and Windows | the same | the transfer fails (EFAULT, WSAEINVAL), the re-read fails, dir offline |
| `EIO` on the first read only, Linux and macOS | the first failure offlines the dir, no re-read | 3 failures, each re-read (8 MiB) succeeds, dir online |
| `EIO` on the first read only, OpenBSD | the first failure offlines the dir, no re-read | not run |
| `EIO` on the first read only, Windows | the disk driver retries the read, which succeeds: no failure reaches Kafka, dir online | not run |

Every run that offlined the directory logged exactly one ERROR from
`LogDirFailureChannel`. On Linux and macOS the consumer read all 20000
records, from broker 2 once the directory was offline; the single
nodes on OpenBSD and Windows have no other replica. In the five-minute
TLS disconnect stress with a healthy disk (177 consumers started and
killed after 2 to 8 seconds on Linux, 178 on macOS), the scheduler of
broker 1 read no segment file and no directory went offline. All of
this matches the runs of 73fc46a880; a known read failure is now
reported inline, and an offline directory no longer logs an ERROR for
later failures.

* Checkstyle, spotless, spotbugs and the javadoc of `clients` pass.

commit.message:
KAFKA-16304: Report file read errors from SslTransportLayer.transferFrom as such

Follow-up to #23445, under the same ticket (resolved, fix version
4.5.0).

Since #23445, a failed send of fetched records is passed to a handler
that re-reads the region on the scheduler, and the log directory is
offlined only if the re-read fails too. The re-read is needed because
over PLAINTEXT `sendfile` reads the file and writes the socket in one
call, so a disk error and a socket error are the same bare
`IOException`. `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` does not have that
problem: it reads the file with `FileChannel.read`, then encrypts and
writes, so it knows which of the two failed. As discussed on #23445,
this passes that on instead of finding it out again:

* `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` throws a new `FileReadException`, an
  `IOException` with the position of the read, when `FileChannel.read`
  or `FileChannel.size` fails. A `ClosedChannelException`, from a
  deletion or a shutdown, is rethrown as is.
* `TransferableChannel.reportsFileReadFailures()` says whether a
  transport does that: true for TLS, false, the default, for
  PLAINTEXT.
* `FileRecords.writeTo` passes a `FileReadException` to the handler,
  and any other failure only if the transport cannot tell the two
  apart. A failure of its own `channel.size()` call before the transfer
  becomes a `FileReadException` as well.
* `LocalLog` reports a `FileReadException` as a failure of the log
  directory without re-reading the region, on the scheduler and at most
  one report at a time per log directory, as for the re-read. Reports
  are tracked apart from re-reads, so that a re-read running in the
  same directory does not drop a known failure. Other failures are
  re-read as before.

Consequences worth stating:

* On TLS listeners a disconnect no longer re-reads the region that was
  being sent. In the test notes, consumers killed mid-fetch over TLS
  for 5 minutes made the scheduler re-read 151 MB without this change
  and nothing with it.
* On TLS listeners a read error now offlines the log directory even if
  the region could be read again by the time of a re-read, e.g. after a
  transient media error. Before, such an error was attributed to the
  socket. This is the criterion `LocalLog` applies to any other
  `IOException`.
* A failed `FileChannel.size()` call on the segment, over either
  transport, is now reported as a read failure without a re-read.
* PLAINTEXT listeners still re-read: `sendfile` cannot tell the two
  apart.
* KRaft snapshots, sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, are still not
  covered.

KAFKA-16304: Report a known read failure without the scheduler

A FileReadException from a transfer now takes the log dir offline right
away, on the network thread, instead of through a task on the scheduler
that was limited to one at a time per log dir. To keep the failures
that follow from flooding the log, LogDirFailureChannel now logs only
the failure that takes a log dir offline. This removes
tryStartReadFailureReport and finishReadFailureReport. The re-read
after any other transfer failure stays on the scheduler, as on trunk.

KAFKA-16304: Wrap failed reads with FileReadException.ofReadFailure

The rule that a ClosedChannelException is rethrown as is and any other
failed read is wrapped in a FileReadException was spelled out in three

+package org.apache.kafka.common.network;
+
+import java.io.IOException;
+import java.nio.channels.ClosedChannelException;
+
+/**
+ * Thrown when a file being transferred to a network channel cannot be read, as opposed to the network channel
+ * failing to be written to. Failing to get the size of the file counts as failing to read it. It is thrown by
+ * {@link TransferableChannel#transferFrom} if the channel {@link TransferableChannel#distinguishesFileReadFailures()},
+ * and by {@link org.apache.kafka.common.record.internal.FileRecords#writeTo} if it cannot get the size of the file
+ * before the transfer. A file closed concurrently, for instance by a deletion or a shutdown, is not a failed read: its
+ * {@link ClosedChannelException} is thrown as it is, see {@link #ofReadFailure}.
+ */
+public class FileReadException extends IOException {
+    private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
+
+    private final long position;
+
+    /**
+     * @param position The absolute position in the file at which the failed read started, or, if the size of the file
+     *                 could not be read, at which the transfer was to start
+     * @param cause The failure of the read
+     */
+    public FileReadException(long position, IOException cause) {
+        super("Failed to read the file at position " + position, cause);
+        this.position = position;
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * @return The absolute position in the file at which the failed read started, or, if the size of the file could
+     *         not be read, at which the transfer was to start
+     */
+    public long position() {
+        return position;
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Returns the exception to throw when a read of a file being transferred to a network channel fails: the failure
+     * itself if it is a {@link ClosedChannelException}, since a file closed concurrently, for instance by a deletion or
+     * a shutdown, says nothing about the medium; otherwise a FileReadException with the failure as its cause.
+     *
+     * @param position The absolute position in the file at which the failed read started, or, if the size of the file
+     *                 could not be read, at which the transfer was to start
+     * @param failure The failure of the read
+     */
+    public static IOException ofReadFailure(long position, IOException failure) {
+        return failure instanceof ClosedChannelException ? failure : new FileReadException(position, failure);
+    }
+}

timeline.message:
KAFKA-16304: Report file read errors from SslTransportLayer.transferFrom as such

Follow-up to #23445, under the same ticket (resolved, fix version
4.5.0).

Since #23445, a failed send of fetched records is passed to a handler
that re-reads the region on the scheduler, and the log directory is
offlined only if the re-read fails too. The re-read is needed because
over PLAINTEXT `sendfile` reads the file and writes the socket in one
call, so a disk error and a socket error are the same bare
`IOException`. `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` does not have that
problem: it reads the file with `FileChannel.read`, then encrypts and
writes, so it knows which of the two failed. As discussed on #23445,
this passes that on instead of finding it out again:

* `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` throws a new `FileReadException`, an
  `IOException` with the position of the read, when `FileChannel.read`
  or `FileChannel.size` fails. A `ClosedChannelException`, from a
  deletion or a shutdown, is rethrown as is.
* `TransferableChannel.reportsFileReadFailures()` says whether a
  transport does that: true for TLS, false, the default, for
  PLAINTEXT.
* `FileRecords.writeTo` passes a `FileReadException` to the handler,
  and any other failure only if the transport cannot tell the two
  apart. A failure of its own `channel.size()` call before the transfer
  becomes a `FileReadException` as well.
* `LocalLog` reports a `FileReadException` as a failure of the log
  directory without re-reading the region, on the scheduler and at most
  one report at a time per log directory, as for the re-read. Reports
  are tracked apart from re-reads, so that a re-read running in the
  same directory does not drop a known failure. Other failures are
  re-read as before.

Consequences worth stating:

* On TLS listeners a disconnect no longer re-reads the region that was
  being sent. In the test notes, consumers killed mid-fetch over TLS
  for 5 minutes made the scheduler re-read 151 MB without this change
  and nothing with it.
* On TLS listeners a read error now offlines the log directory even if
  the region could be read again by the time of a re-read, e.g. after a
  transient media error. Before, such an error was attributed to the
  socket. This is the criterion `LocalLog` applies to any other
  `IOException`.
* A failed `FileChannel.size()` call on the segment, over either
  transport, is now reported as a read failure without a re-read.
* PLAINTEXT listeners still re-read: `sendfile` cannot tell the two
  apart.
* KRaft snapshots, sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, are still not
  covered.

issue.title: KAFKA-16304: Offline the log directory on a disk error in the zero-copy Fetch path

labels.name: storage
labels.description: Pull requests that target the storage module

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
The Fetch response is sent zero copy: the records are read from the
segment by `FileRecords.writeTo`, on the network thread, while the
response is written to the socket. A failed read of the medium and a
client that went away both arrive there as a bare `IOException`, and
`Selector` treats every one of them as a disconnect. A disk error on
this path therefore never offlines the log directory, unlike an I/O
error in the `LocalLog` operations.

This change offlines it, with the same split as elsewhere in the log:
the layer that sees the `IOException` reports it, and storage decides.

* `LocalLog.read` gives the `FileRecords` slices it returns a transfer
  failure handler.
* When the transfer fails, `FileRecords.writeTo` passes the region it
  was writing to the handler and rethrows the original exception
  unchanged. A `ClosedChannelException` is not passed on: the file was
  not read.
* The handler re-reads the region on the log's scheduler, at most once
  at a time per log directory, and calls
  `LogDirFailureChannel.maybeAddOfflineLogDir` only if the read fails,
  with the failed transfer attached. As the log cleaner does, the
  directory is offlined and the error is not rethrown.

The network thread does no extra I/O on a failed send. The send itself
is logged as a disconnect, at DEBUG; the ERROR comes from
`LogDirFailureChannel`.

The classification is as accurate as what the JVM reports, and no more.
Nothing below the JVM is second-guessed: a transient media error that
has cleared by the time of the re-read is attributed to the socket, and
a read that fails for a reason other than the medium is treated as a
storage failure, the criterion `LocalLog` already applies. At the JVM
level, the re-read of the region:

* reads completely: the socket was at fault;
* reaches the end of the file: the log was truncated concurrently (e.g.
  the replica became a follower);
* makes no progress: nothing can be concluded;
* fails with `ClosedChannelException` or a subclass: the segment was
  closed or deleted concurrently, which says nothing about the medium
  (the reasoning of KAFKA-19571);
* fails with any other `IOException`: the log directory is offlined.

The whole region is re-read rather than its first byte because,
depending on the platform, the transfer can fail anywhere within it
without reporting progress: on macOS both `sendfile(2)` and `read(2)`
drop the partial progress of a chunk whose read fails, and on Windows
the JDK does not use `TransmitFile` for a non-blocking socket and falls
back to a mapped buffer or `ReadFile`. On Linux the transfer fails at
the first unreadable page. The re-read reads at most what the failed
call was about to send. The message text of the exception is not
inspected: it is platform specific.

Once the directory is offline its segments are closed, and the next
Fetch gets `KAFKA_STORAGE_ERROR`.

Consequences worth stating:

* A broker whose only log directory, or whose metadata log directory,
  fails on this path now shuts down, as it does today for any other I/O
  error in that directory.
* The KRaft metadata log is read through `LocalLog` too. A read failure
  while the leader sends it marks the raft log's directory offline, the
  next append on the leader fails, and the raft I/O thread's fatal fault
  handler stops the node, as it does today for an I/O error in
  `LocalLog.read` on the metadata log.
* The checks run on the broker's shared background scheduler (the raft
  manager's own scheduler for the metadata log).
* KRaft snapshots are sent through `UnalignedFileRecords`, which this
  change does not cover; I will follow up separately.
* On TLS listeners a read error does not reach `FileRecords` today:
  `SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` swallows it and sends a stale buffer
  instead (KAFKA-21280, #23832). This change takes effect on TLS
  listeners once that is fixed.

timeline.body:
Test notes, continued: the same on macOS 26.7 (Apple Silicon, JDK 17),
with the brokers as local processes, on 73fc46a880 and on trunk
d18f93f985.

* Persistent media error: broker 1's log directory is on a disk image,
  and a 1 MiB band of the image in the middle of the segment is made
  unreadable, so the kernel fails reads of it with EIO. macOS ejects
  the image right after, so every later read fails too. Over TLS,
  trunk re-reads the region on the scheduler, which fails; this change
  offlines the directory without a re-read. Over PLAINTEXT both
  re-read, and the re-read fails. The directory goes offline in all
  four runs, and the consumer reads all 20000 records from broker 2.
* Error gone on the next read, injected by an interposer on `pread`
  and `sendfile` (`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, the macOS stand-in for
  `strace -e inject`): as on Linux, trunk re-reads 8 MiB after each
  failure and keeps the directory online; over TLS this change
  offlines it; over PLAINTEXT both keep it online.
* Disconnects, 3 TLS consumers killed mid-fetch for 5 minutes, about
  180 times: trunk 19497 reads of segment files on the scheduler,
  636 MB; this change none.

On macOS a read fails before the unreadable bytes: with the band at
positions 3129344 to 4177919, `pread` failed at 2129920, and
`sendfile` at 2736128 after reporting progress up to that page. So
`FileReadException.position()` is where the failed read started,
which is not necessarily where the medium failed.

Test notes, continued: OpenBSD 8.0 (arm64, QEMU on macOS) and Windows
10 LTSC (x86-64, QEMU/KVM), both with JDK 17, on 73fc46a880 and on
trunk d18f93f985. Each VM runs one broker and controller, with t1-0 on
a data disk behind QEMU's blkdebug, which fails reads of the disk
sector holding position 4 MiB of the segment with EIO: every read, or
only the first one. A consumer reads the partition from the beginning.

* TLS, every read fails: on both, the network thread's read fails at
  position 4194304. Trunk re-reads the region on the scheduler (3.0 MB
  on OpenBSD, 3.6 MB on Windows), the re-read fails too, and the
  directory goes offline; this change offlines it without a re-read.
* TLS, only the first read fails: on OpenBSD trunk re-reads the region
  successfully and keeps the directory online, while this change
  offlines it. On Windows the disk driver retries the failed read
  (System event 153) and the retry succeeds, so the JVM never sees an
  error, and both keep the directory online.
* PLAINTEXT, every read fails: the JDK writes the file to the socket
  from a memory mapping on both, and the write fails with EFAULT ("Bad
  address") on OpenBSD and WSAEINVAL ("An invalid argument was
  supplied") on Windows rather than with an I/O error. Trunk and this
  change both re-read the region, the re-read fails, and the directory
  goes offline.

No InternalError was thrown in any run.

Windows is on a best-effort basis today. Too different memory management/disk read error handling by the NT kernel and surrounding libraries. 

I will probably take a deeper look after this PR. Maybe, we can bring some better support for Windows.
